articleTitle: Ring cameras go mobile as Amazon debuts AI-powered security drone and robot
summary: Amazon announced Ring Drone Cam and Ring Rover Cam, mobile security devices that use AI Pilot, on-device sensors and cloud processing to map indoor spaces and navigate patrol routes, with targeted availability on January 27, 2027, and shipping on December 16, 2026, respectively. The article contrasts Amazon’s privacy claims with operational restrictions, the drone’s pending FCC authorization, EFF criticism of Ring’s encryption and surveillance practices, and a 2023 FTC investigation describing employee access to private recordings and safeguards that allowed hackers to access 55,000 US customers’ accounts.

deviceA.name: Ring Drone Cam
specs: Flying indoor security camera.
148-degree field of view.
360-degree rotation.
2K video resolution.
Two LED lights activate in low-light conditions.
Limited to 8 minutes of flight time on a new, fully-charged battery under controlled conditions.
Includes a charging docking station.
AI Pilot uses cameras, specialized vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing.
Setup requires the customer to carry the drone through indoor spaces so AI Pilot can digitally map the floor plan.
AI Pilot can supposedly identify rooms and suggest patrol points near doors, windows or sensitive business locations.
Can supposedly follow a set route and schedule for Ring Protect subscribers.
Can automatically fly set routes in response to a notification from a Ring camera, sensor or alarm.
Can be controlled directly from Alexa Home Map.
Navigation performance may degrade around reflective surfaces such as polished marble or wet tile, featureless blank matte walls, or transparent surfaces such as frameless glass and mirrors.
Physical dimensions, battery capacity, charging duration, quantified coverage area and a specific floor-count restriction are not stated in the supplied article.
deviceA.availability: Amazon aims for January 27, 2027, contingent on FCC authorization; customers can register for email updates.

deviceB.name: Ring Rover Cam
specs: Wheeled autonomous security robot designed for business.
Livestreams and records in up to 4K video resolution.
Can perform a 360-degree scan at a designated location.
AI Pilot uses cameras, specialized vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing.
Autonomous exploration during setup allows AI Pilot to digitally map the floor plan.
Automatically responds to connected Ring-device alerts by following preprogrammed patrol points.
Designed for a single-floor, indoor environment; cannot climb stairs.
Not compatible with curved edges, sunken areas, flooring transitions greater than 1.375 inches (3.5 centimeters), or black glossy floors.
Automatically adjustable mast allows the camera to peer over counters, shelving and other obstacles.
Claimed coverage of up to 5,000 square feet (465 square meters).
Includes a siren and light tower.
Includes a microphone for two-way audio communication.
Doorbell-ring, motion-event and Live View event videos are stored in the cloud for sharing and replaying for up to 180 days.
Physical dimensions, mast height, battery life, battery capacity and charging duration are not stated in the supplied article.
deviceB.availability: Already available for preorder; scheduled to start shipping on December 16, 2026.

coreControversy.corporateClaim: Amazon describes Ring Robotics as offering “privacy and security without compromise,” citing LED indicators and screen notifications when video and audio recording are active. Amazon also says videos from both devices will be protected by Throw Away the Key Encryption, introduced in September 2026.
coreControversy.criticismOrAlarm: EFF describes Throw Away the Key Encryption as an improvement over Ring’s former default settings but still well short of end-to-end encryption. EFF also criticizes Jamie Siminoff’s approach and Ring’s reintroduction of features allowing law enforcement to request footage or live-stream access from users’ home security devices. The article warns that mobile AI-enabled cameras could create additional privacy risks.
coreControversy.regulatoryOrHistoricalPrecedent: In a 2023 FTC investigation, Ring was charged with allowing employees and contractors to watch recordings of customers’ private spaces; the FTC also described safeguards that allowed hackers to access 55,000 US customers’ accounts. Ring Always Home Cam previously prompted privacy concerns, with University of Washington researcher Ryan Calo describing additional opportunities for indoor surveillance and corporate access to sensitive or identifying details of homes and businesses. Ring’s Familiar Faces feature, available for fixed Ring doorbell cameras starting in December 2025, is already the subject of a class action lawsuit. The article does not identify facial recognition as a feature of the new robots.

hiddenCatchesAndLimits: AI Pilot uses cloud processing as well as on-device sensors; the described system is not local-only.
Both devices digitally map the customer’s home or business floor plan during setup.
The article explicitly ties the drone’s set-route and scheduled operation to a Ring Protect subscription; it does not specify a subscription price or a Rover-specific subscription requirement.
Ring Drone Cam still requires FCC authorization before going on sale, making January 27, 2027, a conditional availability target.
The drone’s 8 minutes of flight time is specified for a new, fully-charged battery under controlled conditions.
Drone navigation may degrade around polished marble, wet tile, featureless blank matte walls, frameless glass and mirrors.
Rover is restricted to a single-floor, indoor environment and cannot climb stairs.
Rover is incompatible with curved edges, sunken areas, flooring transitions greater than 1.375 inches (3.5 centimeters), and black glossy floors.
Rover coverage is claimed to be up to 5,000 square feet (465 square meters), not an independently verified performance result.
Rover videos triggered by doorbell rings, motion events and Live View events are stored in the cloud for up to 180 days.
The article does not specify a separate drone video-retention period or an encryption-key retention or deletion schedule.
EFF says Throw Away the Key Encryption remains well short of end-to-end encryption despite improving on Ring’s former default settings.
The article makes no claim that the new robots implement facial recognition or similar AI-powered identification of people.
The supplied article does not provide physical dimensions for either device or battery-life specifications for Rover.
